capitals.note: Republic restored 31 December 1813; in the years 1798-1813 Geneva was capital of the French département du Léman.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria shape (the swiss-confederation dossier notes Cliopatria draws Geneva as Swiss only 1540-1571). The infobox gives no area and the History of Geneva page none; the Republic was a city-state of a few hundred km2, about one 253 km2 cell at the grid resolution, so a 10 km radius around Geneva is drawn. The Bernese-held 'lands of Savoy in the Genevan basin (including all the Pays de Gex)' of 1536-1564 were Savoy's, not Geneva's.

region.text: Geneva and the mandements that depended on the Bishop

ledger.note: 1534: Geneva declares itself independent of bishop and duke. Infobox 'Independence from the Prince-Bishopric of Geneva: 1534'; 'declaration of independence from episcopal and Savoyard authority' in 1534, the authorities 'declared in October of the same year the vacancy of the Bishopric'. The History of Geneva page has the bishop's final flight in July 1533 and the Reformation made official on 21 May 1536. The page names the city and mandements, not a boundary.

region.text: Geneva, associate state of the Old Swiss Confederacy

ledger.note: 1534: Geneva is an associate state of the Old Swiss Confederacy from its birth. Republic of Geneva page infobox: 'Associate state of the Old Swiss Confederacy'; 'The treaty was ratified in Geneva in February 1526, despite the protests of the bishop Pierre de la Baume and the Mammelus' (the alliance with Bern and Fribourg, eight years before the independence); 'As a response, the Catholic Canton of Fribourg broke its alliance with the city'; 'Geneva obtains the alliance with Zürich in 1584.' The Old Swiss Confederacy page lists the Republic of Geneva among the associates with a '1536 treaty with Bern and a 1584 treaty with Zürich and Bern' and no 1526 treaty. Mirror of swiss-confederation /ledger/29, which starts the tint in February 1526 before this state exists; the associate tint here starts at the founding, 1534, with the 1526 alliance already in force (confidence 2: the page gives the status without a year of its own). The swiss-confederation owner should move /ledger/29 from 1526 to 1534, or to 1536 if it prefers the Old Swiss Confederacy page's treaty with Bern. An alliance, not subjection: the nearest rule-4 tint.

region.text: Cartigny, Jussy, Vandoeuvres, Gy and some other smaller territories

ledger.note: 1754: a treaty with Savoy adds territory. 'In a similar treaty with Savoy in 1754, Geneva received from Savoy Cartigny, Jussy, Vandoeuvres, Gy, and some other smaller territories.' The page does not name the treaty; Savoy's state in 1754 is the Kingdom of Sardinia. The circle is the researcher's reading of four villages close to the city.

region.text: Geneva and its territory, annexed by France

ledger.note: 15 April 1798: France annexes Geneva. Infobox 'Annexation by France: 15 April 1798'; 'The wish would be granted on 15 April 1798 when the Genevan government is coerced by economic and political pressure to request the annexation by France'; Geneva 'is then made capital of a new département du Léman'. The History of Geneva page says only 'In 1798 ... France, then under the Directory, annexed Geneva'. The french-directory dossier dates the same gain to 26 August 1798.

15 April 1798: the association ends with the annexation. Infobox 'Annexation by France: 15 April 1798'; 'The wish would be granted on 15 April 1798 when the Genevan government is coerced by economic and political pressure to request the annexation by France'; the Old Swiss Confederacy page says Geneva and Mulhouse remained associates 'until events of the French Revolutionary Wars in 1798'. Mirror of swiss-confederation /ledger/41, same month as the loss to France above (french-directory /ledger/17 has 26 August 1798; the Republic of Geneva page does not give that date).

31 December 1813: the Republic is restored. Infobox 'Restoration of the Republic: 31 December 1813'; the French army left 'on 30 December 1813' and 'on the next day the return of the Republic (Restauration de la République) was proclaimed'; the History of Geneva page credits the Austrian general Ferdinand von Bubna und Littitz.

19 May 1815: Geneva joins the Swiss Confederation. Infobox 'Accession to the Swiss Confederation: 19 May 1815'; 'Geneva was admitted as a canton to the Swiss Confederation'. The Congress of Vienna then extended Geneva 'to cover fifteen Savoyard and six French parishes' (Treaty of Turin, 16 March 1816); those parishes belong to the canton's later ledger.
1815: the Republic of Geneva becomes the canton of Geneva. The Republic's own life ends with its accession.

wars.name: Bernese-French campaign against Savoy

zones.text: the lands of Savoy in the Genevan basin (including all the Pays de Gex)

wars.outcome: 'A new army of Bernese in alliance with France defeated Savoy' after Savoy's attempt of 1535-36, and occupied 'the lands of Savoy in the Genevan basin'; Savoy recovered them by the Treaty of Lausanne of 1564 while 'losing forever the Pays de Vaud to Bern'.
wars.note: The occupied land was Savoy's, not Geneva's; it is listed for the frontier it created round the city.

wars.name: Escalade and Treaty of Saint-Julien
wars.outcome: The Escalade of 1602 ended with the Treaty of Saint-Julien (21 July 1603), which bars Geneva from 'building any military facilities and from keeping any garrison on a 15-km radius around the city'. No border change.
wars.note: The page dates the Escalade only as 1602 and the treaty to 'July the same year' in the text but 21 July 1603 in the infobox; the infobox year is used.

certainty.note: A city-state with scattered mandements and a frontier that Bern and Savoy fought over in 1535-1564; no survey on the pages.
Sharp from the 1754 treaty that gave Geneva named parishes; the French years 1798-1813 are not Geneva's.

notes: No Cliopatria row: every keyframe is new. One dossier covers the Republic before 1798 and the Restored Republic of 1813-1815, with the French years 1798-1813 as a gap (loss and gain events); a gap-filler could split them if the renderer cannot hold a state across a gap. The Republic's territory is a 10 km circle: neither page gives an area or a list of mandements beyond Satigny, Peney, Jussy and the four 1754 villages; the 1749 exchange with France is on the page ('the Republic and France exchanged territories in that year') but what changed hands is not stated, so it has no event. Dates disagree: annexation 15 April 1798 (this page, infobox) against 26 August 1798 in the french-directory dossier; the swiss-confederation dossier ends its associate tint in April 1798 and starts it in 1526 (ratified February 1526), eight years before this Republic's 1534 independence, and also says 'No Cliopatria shape contains Geneva after 1571'. The Prince-Bishopric of Geneva (predecessor, dates not on the pages) has no dossier. Gazetteer names needed: none (Geneva place and the circle cover it). Repair 2026-11-01: the associate tint of the Old Swiss Confederacy is now in the ledger (vassal_start 1534, vassal_end April 1798) as a mirror of swiss-confederation /ledger/29 and /41. The Swiss event starts in February 1526, before this state exists; the Geneva page gives the 1526 treaty with Bern and Fribourg, the Old Swiss Confederacy page a 1536 treaty with Bern and a 1584 treaty with Zürich and Bern. The tint here starts at the founding in 1534; the swiss-confederation owner should move /ledger/29 to 1534. The 1754 additions add no cell to the 10 km circle, so they need no separate tint event.
